issues.problem: The piece presents the first-seven-week ratio of 'between eight and nine times' as Snow's conclusion, and the story ends there. The evidence shows this was an interim result. Snow states that the gap narrowed as the epidemic advanced. It was fourteen times in the first four weeks and nearly five times in the second seven weeks. Over the whole 14 weeks it was 153 against 26 deaths per 10,000 living. As written, the piece mistakes a midpoint for the outcome. The en and zh versions share this omission.

evidence.quote: became not quite so great, although it continued very striking
The cholera was therefore fourteen times as fatal at this period
continued to suffer nearly five times the mortality of that supplied with water by the Lambeth Company
Houses supplied by Lambeth Company 173,748 461 26

issues.proposed: State that 'eight to nine times' applies only to the first seven weeks. Add one sentence in both languages: Snow wrote that the gap narrowed as the epidemic advanced, to nearly five times in the second seven weeks (537 against 115 per 10,000 houses). Over the 14 weeks to 14 October it was 153 against 26 per 10,000 living, which was still lower than London at large but not lower than the north and central districts. Use only clearly legible figures, such as 537/115 and 153/26. Do not cite the garbled '2,8S0'.
issues.rationale: 中英文都改为说明“八到九倍”只是疫情头七周的结果。补充了斯诺自己说的差距随疫情推进而缩小，并补上清楚可辨的数字：头四周每万户71对5（十四倍），第二个七周每万户537对115（接近五倍），截至10月14日的14周每万居民153对26，低于全伦敦但不低于北区和中区。未引用乱码数字。ev 增加 W-E14、W-E15、W-E17。

issues.problem: The paragraph says there was no independent check and that one man ran the inquiry and compiled the statistics. Two points in the evidence contradict this. (1) The registrar returns were actually made after 26 August. They were incomplete, but Snow reports that they 'agree entirely' with his earlier results. (2) Part of the inquiry, in Bermondsey and other districts supplied only by Southwark and Vauxhall, was done by Mr. John Joseph Whiting, not by Snow himself. Note that both facts are known only from Snow's own book.

evidence.quote: the Registrar General requested the District Registrars to make a return of the water supply of the house of attack in all cases of death from cholera
the water supply remained unascertained in a number of cases
they agree entirely with the results of my inquiry respecting the earlier part of the epidemic given above
I was fortunate enough to obtain the assistance of a medical man, Mr. John Joseph Whiting, L.A.C., to make inquiry in Bermondsey

issues.proposed: Rewrite as follows. The returns that district registrars made after 26 August at the Registrar General's request were incomplete, with some cases unascertained, but Snow says they 'agree entirely' with his results. This counts as partial corroboration from registration data, though it reaches us only through Snow's book. Inquiries in Bermondsey and certain other districts were made by the medical man John Joseph Whiting. Delete 'the same man ... conducts the inquiry' and keep the reminder that we are reading one side's record.
issues.rationale: 删去“没有独立核查”和“同一个人做调查”的说法。改为：8月26日以后各区登记员确实填报了供水，数据不完整，但斯诺称与他的结果完全一致，算部分印证，且只经斯诺的书得知；伯蒙德西等只由南华克和沃克斯霍尔供水的地区由怀廷医生调查。保留“读到的是一方的记录”的提醒。ev 增加 W-E11、W-E13、W-E16。

issues.problem: The piece says Snow's method yielded 'a comparison of two waters within the same streets' (zh: 在同一批街道里比较两种水). This conflicts with story.7 and with the evidence. Table IX covers all houses supplied by each company, not only the intermixed streets. Snow extended the inquiry to every district supplied by either company because there were no per-district household counts. Only the Kennington-type data are within the same streets, and those are counts, not death rates.

evidence.quote: as the number of houses which they supplied in particular districts was not stated

issues.proposed: Change to: 'in return he obtained counts of deaths by water supply for houses in the same intermixed streets, and a company-wide comparison per 10,000 houses'. Alternatively, add 'partly' so that it matches the reservation in story.7.

edits.after: 疫情头七周的结果，他整理成一张表。南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水40,046户，霍乱死亡1,263人；兰贝斯公司供水26,107户，死亡98人；伦敦其余地区256,423户，死亡1,422人。折算成每10,000户的死亡数，分别是315、37和59。他据此得出结论：南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水户的死亡率是兰贝斯公司供水户的八到九倍。但这只是疫情头七周的结果。斯诺自己说明，随着疫情推进，两组的悬殊“没那么大了”，不过仍然十分显著。疫情头四周是每万户71对5，相差十四倍；第二个七周是每万户537对115，接近五倍。截至10月14日的14周里，按每万居民计，南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水户死亡153人，兰贝斯公司供水户死亡26人。兰贝斯供水户的死亡率低于全伦敦，但并不低于北区和中区。

edits.before: The first seven weeks of the epidemic went into a single table. Houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company: 40,046, with 1,263 deaths from cholera. Lambeth Company: 26,107 houses, 98 deaths. The rest of London: 256,423 houses, 1,422 deaths. Per 10,000 houses that came to 315, 37 and 59. Snow's conclusion: "The mortality in the houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company was therefore between eight and nine times as great as in the houses supplied by the Lambeth Company".
edits.after: The first seven weeks of the epidemic went into a single table. Houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company: 40,046, with 1,263 deaths from cholera. Lambeth Company: 26,107 houses, 98 deaths. The rest of London: 256,423 houses, 1,422 deaths. Per 10,000 houses that came to 315, 37 and 59. Snow's conclusion: "The mortality in the houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company was therefore between eight and nine times as great as in the houses supplied by the Lambeth Company". That was the figure for the first seven weeks only. Snow himself wrote that as the epidemic advanced the disproportion "became not quite so great, although it continued very striking". In the first four weeks it had been 71 against 5 per 10,000 houses, fourteen times. In the second seven weeks it was 537 against 115 per 10,000 houses, nearly five times. Over the 14 weeks ending 14 October, there were 153 deaths per 10,000 living in houses supplied by Southwark and Vauxhall and 26 in houses supplied by Lambeth. The Lambeth figure was lower than London at large, but not lower than the north and central districts.

edits.before: 必须说清楚：本篇所有数字与叙述都出自斯诺本人的书和表格，本篇的证据里没有当时卫生部门或第三方的独立核查。死者住址来自登记总署，8月26日以后的供水信息按要求应由各区登记员填报；但本篇读到的统计和论证都经斯诺之手整理。提出学说、做调查、整理统计的是同一个人，这不意味着数据有错，但意味着我们读到的是一方的记录。
edits.after: 必须说清楚：本篇所有数字与叙述都出自斯诺本人的书和表格。死者住址来自登记总署。8月26日以后，各区登记员应登记总长的要求，填报了霍乱死亡病例发病房屋的供水情况。这些填报并不完整，仍有一批个案的供水没有查明。斯诺写道，这些填报与他对疫情早期的调查结果“完全一致”。这算是来自登记数据的部分印证，不过我们也只是通过斯诺的书才知道这一点。另外，调查并非全部出自斯诺之手：伯蒙德西等一些只由南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水的地区，是由医生约翰·约瑟夫·怀廷（John Joseph Whiting）去调查的。即便如此，学说、统计和呈现它们的这本书都出自斯诺。这不意味着数据有错，但意味着我们读到的是一方的记录。

edits.before: Plainly: every figure and every account in this piece comes from Snow's own book and his own tables, and the evidence used here contains no independent check by a health authority or anyone else at the time. The addresses of the dead came from the General Register Office, and after 26 August the registrars were asked to return the water supply; but the statistics and the argument we read here were all put together by Snow. When the same man proposes the doctrine, conducts the inquiry and presents the statistics, that does not make the data wrong, but it does mean we are reading one side's record.
edits.after: Plainly: every figure and every account in this piece comes from Snow's own book and his own tables. The addresses of the dead came from the General Register Office. After 26 August the district registrars, at the Registrar General's request, returned the water supply of the house of attack in cholera deaths. The returns were incomplete, and the supply "remained unascertained in a number of cases". Even so, Snow says they "agree entirely" with the results of his inquiry into the earlier part of the epidemic. That is partial corroboration from registration data, though it reaches us only through Snow's book. Nor was the whole inquiry Snow's own work. A medical man, John Joseph Whiting, made the inquiries in Bermondsey and certain other districts supplied only by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company. Still, the doctrine, the statistics and the book that presents them are all Snow's. That does not make the data wrong, but it does mean we are reading one side's record.

edits.before: Another approach, and this is the author's counterfactual rather than history, would have been to compare average death rates by district, or rich districts against poor ones. Wealth, housing and occupation would then have crowded in, and the effect of the water would have been hard to separate out. What Snow actually did was more laborious — death addresses, house by house, water carried home in phials — and in return he got a comparison of two waters within the same streets.
edits.after: Another approach, and this is the author's counterfactual rather than history, would have been to compare average death rates by district, or rich districts against poor ones. Wealth, housing and occupation would then have crowded in, and the effect of the water would have been hard to separate out. What Snow actually did was more laborious: death addresses, house by house, and water carried home in phials. In return he got two things. One was counts of deaths by water supply for houses in the same intermixed streets. The other was a company-wide comparison per 10,000 houses.
